reason: Both satisfy the hard requirements, but Response B is more operationally robust: it addresses the edge case where snapshot capacity is itself constrained by the near-full disk (snapshotting to a separate target), proposes throttling write traffic instead of touching the DB if disk nears 100% before the snapshot finishes, and its abort/rollback condition specifies concrete reversal actions (restore from snapshot, resume only-if-safe) rather than just escalation. It also separates WAL/temp volume checks and requires verified replica disk headroom before failover, closing gaps Response A leaves more implicit.
